Welcome to Coston Primary School
COSTON OPEN DAYS 2026
We are delighted that you are thinking of sending your child to Coston Primary School. If you would like to book onto one of our Open Days, please contact the school office on admin@coston.ealing.sch.uk/02085781515 October Wed 7th at 1.45pmThursday 8th at 10amTuesday 13th at 1.45pmThursday 15th at 10amMonday 19th at 1.45pmThursday 22nd at 10amNovemberTuesday 3rd at 1.45pmThursday 5th at 10amMonday 9th at 1.45pmWednesday 18th at 1.45pmFriday 20th at 10amTuesday 24th at 1.45pmThursday 26th at 10am
Headteachers Welcome
Coston is a vibrant, diverse and inclusive school where children are at the heart of everything we do. We are ambitious for every child and committed to providing an education which enables them not only to achieve well academically, but to grow into confident, curious, compassionate and responsible young people. At the heart of our school is a simple belief:Every child belongs. Every child is included. Every child succeeds.
Copyright © 2026 · Legal Information
Primary School Website Design by Greenhouse School Websites
BBC Coverage
Art Showcase - Thursday 23rd October 2025

Core Values
We believe that the child should lie at the heart of our curriculum, and that everything we do should contribute to the full and rounded development of every child, as well as to the acquisition of new skills, knowledge, and understanding. Initially all staff were involved in choosing a set of core values - attributes and behaviours that we want to help everybody at Coston to develop during their time at the school. We believe that these behaviours will help us all to become better lifelong learners, and make Coston a happy and supportive environment for learning. Our core values are:
Children and adults at Coston show respect for one another, for themselves and for their environment. We treat others in the way we would like to be treated. We listen, and we value each other's ideas.
Children and adults at Coston persevere in the face of challenges and stay calm in stressful situations. We take risks and understand the value of making mistakes. We know how to help ourselves when we find something hard. We know that success comes through hardwork and never giving up.
Children and adults at Coston are able to put themselves in other people's shoes and show concern and care for others, both within and outside of the school. We understand that other people may feel differently from themselves. We can put others before ourselves and look after one another.
Children, staff, parents and local community work together as a team and care for each other and help each other to be the best that we can be
Children and adults at Coston are able to reflect and recognise their own strengths and areas of development. Children at Coston are able to think carefully about their learning and actions and know how to make things better.
If you would like to read more about our Core Values please refer to our handbook
Copyright © 2026 · Legal Information
Primary School Website Design by Greenhouse School Websites

British Values
The Department for Education state that there is a need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
At Coston Primary School these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Children have many opportunities for their voices to be heard. We have a school council which meets regularly to discuss issues raised in class. The school council has been created to genuinely effect change within the school. The council members for each year group are voted in by their class.
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safety, through of provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advise how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it be through choice of challenge, of how they record, of participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
Part of our school ethos and behaviour policy has revolved around the value of ‘Respect’, and pupils have been part of discussions and assemblies related to what this means and how it is shown. These assemblies, and PSHCE lessons promote respect for others and this is reiterated through the work in the playground, classroom, learning skills and on the sports field, as well as our behaviour policy.
The pupils know and understand that it is expected and imperative that respect is shown to everyone, whatever differences we may have.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
The value of Respect ensures tolerance of those who have different faiths and beliefs. This is achieved through enhancing pupils understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity. Assemblies and discussions involving prejudices and prejudice-based bullying have been followed and supported by learning in RE and PSHCE. Members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school.
Copyright © 2026 · Legal Information
Primary School Website Design by Greenhouse School Websites

School Ethos
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions any parent has to undertake. At Coston Primary School we believe passionately in providing the correct blend of academic challenge, moral development and enrichment that allows for the holistic development of each child in our care. Your child is as special to us as they are to you and our aim is not to limit, but rather liberate, their potential.
At Coston Primary School the children are at the centre of all decision making and our priority is to deliver high quality teaching and learning whilst at the same time providing rich and truly enjoyable learning experiences for all children.
We believe passionately in the importance of recognising every pupil as a unique individual, each with their own gifts and talents. Our work as teachers begins by building upon the numerous skills you have fostered in your child at home. It is our aim to develop a successful partnership with you so that your child is given every possible opportunity to flourish.
We want every child to be successful; to reach for success from the very first day they join us and throughout their school lives so that when they leave us, they have a love of learning for the rest of their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Coston Primary School - Head Teacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head Teacher's Welcome
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Coston Primary School.
Coston is a vibrant, diverse and inclusive school where children are at the heart of everything we do. We are ambitious for every child and committed to providing an education which enables them not only to achieve well academically, but to grow into confident, curious, compassionate and responsible young people.
At the heart of our school is a simple belief:
Every child belongs. Every child is included. Every child succeeds.
We want every child who comes through our doors to know that they are valued for who they are. Our children bring different cultures, languages, experiences, strengths and needs to our community, and we believe that this diversity makes Coston a richer and stronger place in which to learn and grow.
We have high expectations for children's learning and achievement and provide a broad and ambitious curriculum which gives them the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for the future. Alongside this, we place great importance on the wider experiences of childhood. Through sport, music, the arts, trips and visits, clubs, outdoor play, leadership opportunities and the many other experiences we offer, we want children to discover their interests, develop their talents and experience the joy of learning.
Inclusion is fundamental to who we are. Our school encompasses mainstream provision, specialist provision for children with complex needs and Coston SRP, our Specialist Resourced Provision for autistic children. We are proud to be a community in which children learn alongside one another, difference is understood and celebrated, and support is shaped around the individual child.
We also know that children flourish when school and home work together. We value the relationships we build with our families and recognise the important part that parents and carers play in their children's education. We want Coston to be a community in which families, as well as children, feel welcomed, listened to and that they belong.
Above all, Coston is a happy school. Our children bring energy, character and enthusiasm to it every day, and I feel enormously privileged to be their Head Teacher.
A website can only ever give you a glimpse of what makes a school special. If you are considering Coston for your child, I warmly invite you to come and visit us, meet our children and staff and experience our school for yourself.
I hope you will quickly see what we want every child at Coston to know:
Kate Moyse Head Teacher

Music
At Coston Primary School, we aim to provide an enjoyable and challenging music curriculum that gives all pupils the opportunity to sing, play, create, and perform—both individually and collaboratively. Lessons are inclusive and developmentally appropriate for different age groups and the specific needs of the children, while still offering opportunities for students to stretch and challenge themselves. Our music curriculum is carefully designed to build strong foundations and develop musical skills and knowledge progressively over time. Pupils become confident in their ability to create, compose, perform, and listen with understanding.
Our music curriculum is organised into half-termly units with clear, step-by-step progression. Each unit builds on prior learning, helping children to consolidate knowledge, deepen their understanding, and expand their musical abilities. A structured approach to teaching ensures that new concepts are introduced logically and linked to previous learning experiences. Throughout the year, children regularly have opportunities to perform and reflect on the pieces they have studied. These performances—often at the end of each half term—allow pupils to showcase their learning and provide teachers with valuable insights into student progress.
To read more about Music at Coston click here for the Music Development Plan.

pageCache.text:
Communicating with Parents/Carers (Reach More Parents)
Here at Coston Primary School, we use Reach More Parents as our main source of communication between home and school. Reach More Parents is a digital communications tool which allows you, as parents, to see a wealth of important information concerning your child, right at your fingertips. We use Reach More Parents to inform you about key dates in the term, to keep you up to speed with your child’s learning and for sending out important notices, among many other things.
To get on board with us, download the Reach More Parents app onto your smart phone or tablet or visit https://app.weduc.co.uk/.
You will require an enrolment code to get started, which will be issued to families when they join the school, along with instructions on how to get set up.

Wellbeing
At Coston Primary School, we are committed to supporting the mental health and wellbeing of our whole school community (children, staff, parents and carers), and recognise how important mental health and emotional wellbeing is to our lives.
We have a supportive, caring and respectful ethos, and we strongly believe in the importance of recognising every pupil as a unique individual, each with their own gifts and talents.
The information and resources in this section of our school website are intended to provide support and guidance to our parents and carers. Also, we offer ideas of activities to help to maintain a healthy wellbeing.

Art
At Coston, Art is seen as an important subject which develops concentration, attention, fine motor skills. expression and choice. Art lessons are planned to develop drawing and painting skills, leading to a piece of work focused on a particular art discipline: sculpture, print, textiles or mixed media.
Through each unit, children practise mark-making, honing these skills and applying them appropriately to their sketches and drawings. Children learn to apply watercolour, powder paint and acrylic confidently, developing colour mixing skills and experimenting with shades.
Through exploration of other media, children learn to plan, compose, assemble, join, embellish and enhance using clay, wire, wood, fabric and various forms of print.

Computing & E-Safety
Computing in the 21st Century is seen as an essential resource to support teaching and learning, as well as playing an important role in the everyday lives of children, young people and adults. Consequently, schools need to build in the use of these technologies in order to ensure our young people develop the skills to access life-long learning and employment.
Each class from Years 1-6, has its own complete suite of 30 Chromebooks enabling every child to have access to their own dedicated device with their own Google account. In order to provide remote learning, we use Google Classroom. This digital platform supports the teaching of live lessons, the sharing of resources and enables children to complete and hand-in classwork. Wi-Fi access has been upgraded in all buildings to support multiple devices logging onto the Internet at the same time. Each individual classroom also has its own interactive screen and internet access.
Coston children are encouraged to start computing activities from the Nursery, where an interactive screen and computers are in use from day one. As children progress through the school they have access to a wide variety of information technology resources, where they learn skills such as blogging, coding, 3D-modelling, graphics and storing/retrieving data.
At Coston, we understand the responsibility to educate our children on E-Safety issues; teaching them the appropriate behaviours and critical thinking skills to enable them to remain both safe and legal when using the Internet and related technologies, in and beyond the context of the classroom.
ICT and online resources are increasingly used across the curriculum. We believe it is essential for E-Safety guidance to be given to the children on a regular basis.
